title: Codex Desktop execution context was delivered as repeated monolithic briefs without role routing or measurable budgets
symptoms: Stable governance was repeatedly pasted into task prompts.
Canonical briefs mixed authority, history, implementation, validation and audit context.
Role intent was inferred anew by each Codex Desktop thread.
Line count was used informally without bytes, token estimate or source-load metrics.
Multi-agent use lacked a common risk-based routing and parallelism contract.
corrective_action: Create validated execution envelopes and selective context manifests.
Create lightweight role profiles and risk-based routing.
Define controlled parallelism and context budgets.
Require operational before/after measurement before claiming speed improvement.
